q: A change feed delivers sequence 76 (city Vienna) and then sequence 75 (city Berlin) for the same customer. With `SEQUENCE BY sequence_num` and `STORED AS SCD TYPE 1`, what does the target hold afterwards?
o: Vienna, because sequence 75 is older than the change already applied
The update fails because the events are out of order
e: AUTO CDC keeps the change with the highest sequence value per key. A late event with a lower sequence is ignored in Type 1.

q: In an SCD Type 2 table built by AUTO CDC, how do you select the current version of every customer?
e: Each change closes the previous version by setting `__END_AT`. The open version, with `__END_AT` NULL, is the current one. Deleted keys have no open version.

q: Your `MERGE INTO customers USING changes` fails with an error that several source rows match the same target row. What is the fix?
o: Add `WHEN NOT MATCHED BY SOURCE THEN DELETE`
Switch the target to SCD Type 2
Reduce the source to the latest event per key by sequence before merging
e: MERGE needs at most one source row per target row. Keep only the latest change per key, for example with `QUALIFY row_number() OVER (PARTITION BY key ORDER BY seq DESC) = 1`.

q: A source system cannot produce a change feed. It exports the full product table every night. Which AUTO CDC variant fits?
o: `AUTO CDC INTO` with `SEQUENCE BY` on the export date
AUTO CDC from snapshot, which compares consecutive snapshots to infer inserts, updates and deletes
A materialized view over the latest export
`APPLY AS TRUNCATE WHEN` on every load
e: `create_auto_cdc_from_snapshot_flow` compares each snapshot with the previous one. Keys missing from the new snapshot become deletes.

q: An SCD Type 2 dimension creates a new version every time `last_login` changes, and it grows far too fast. Only `city` and `tier` changes matter for history. What do you change?
e: With `track_history_column_list` (SQL: `TRACK HISTORY ON`), only changes to the listed columns open a new version. Other columns are updated in place on the current row.
